summary: Obfuscated dynamic-eval loader shipped in tarball, not reachable from install or import
details: The published tarball contains api.js at the package root, a heavily obfuscated loader using an obfuscator.io-style XOR-decoded string table (key 0x46) that reconstructs identifiers including 'constructor', stashes require and module on the global object, and uses Function(...) to compile and immediately invoke an approximately 9.6 KB decoded payload. The file is referenced only by the author's manual scripts.build step (node api.js && tsc); it is not referenced by the package's main entry (index.js), not imported by any reachable module, and not invoked by the declared postinstall. The postinstall script performs a local file-copy of vendor/fetch-page-assets/index.ts into node_modules via fs.copyFileSync with no network I/O and no shell exec of api.js. Because the obfuscated loader is dormant on both npm install and require of the package, no installer-harm dataflow is produced in normal consumer use, but shipping an obfuscated dynamic-eval loader with concealed payload contents in a published tarball is an unusual transparency and supply-chain hygiene concern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
